content: When co-administering cenobamate with other drugs, adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Both chlorpromazine and bedaquiline can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring of ECG and potential therapy adjustments. Similarly, ciprofloxacin, citalopram, clarithromycin, clomipramine, clozapine, crizotinib, and other drugs that increase the QTc interval when combined with bedaquiline require close ECG monitoring and therapy modification. Crofeler increases bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut, though systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Dabrafenib decreases bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy adjustments and close monitoring. Dasatinib, degarelix, desipramine, deutetrabenazine, and other QTc-prolonging drugs co-administered with bedaquiline also require close ECG monitoring and therapy modification. Deutetrabenazine, at its maximum recommended dose, does not clinically prolong the QT interval significantly, but caution is advised in certain circumstances that increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or co-administration with other QTc-prolonging drugs. Disopyramide, dofetilide, dolasetron, doxepin, dronedarone, droperidol, and other QTc-prolonging drugs co-administered with bedaquiline require close ECG monitoring and therapy adjustments. Elagolix decreases bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered, and consider dose adjustments. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Co-administration with erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate) and bedaquiline increases the QTc interval, requiring close ECG monitoring and therapy adjustments. Escitalopram, ezogabine, fedratinib, flecainide, floxuridine, fluconazole, fluoxetine, fluphenazine, formoterol, foscarnet, fostemsavir, gemifloxacin, gepirone, goserelin, haloperidol, histrelin, ibutilide, iloperidone, indapamide, isradipine, and other QTc-prolonging drugs co-administered with bedaquiline require close ECG monitoring and therapy adjustments. Iloperidone also increases bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Lapatinib, lenvatinib, leuprolide, levalbuterol, levofloxacin, lopinavir, lumefantrine, maprotiline, mavorixafor, mefloquine, methadone, mifepristone, mitotane, moxifloxacin, nilotinib, nirmatrelvir, and other QTc-prolonging drugs co-administered with bedaquiline require close ECG monitoring and therapy adjustments. Mifepristone increases bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concurrent use of bedaquiline for more than 14 days unless benefits outweigh risks. Mitotane decreases bedaquiline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for potential dosage adjustments. Osilodrostat, osimertinib, oxaliplatin, ozanimod, paliperidone, pasireotide, pazopanib, pentamidine, perphenazine, pimozide, posaconazole, procainamide, propafenone, protriptyline, quetiapine, quinidine, quinine, quizartinib, ranolazine, risperidone, romidepsin, rucaparib, selpercatinib, sertraline, solifenacin, sorafenib, sotalol, stiripentol, sunitinib, tacrolimus, tazemetostat, tecovirimat, telavancin, thioridazine, thiothixene, toremifene, trimipramine, triptorelin, valbenazine, vandetanib, vardenafil, vemurafenib, voclosporin, voriconazole, vorinostat, and ziprasidone all increase the QTc interval when co-administered with bedaquiline. Therapy adjustments and close ECG monitoring are required. Acetazolamide, anastrozole, cyclophosphamide, danazol, drospirenone, larotrectinib, and other drugs may increase bedaquiline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, though the clinical significance is unknown. Adagrasib, albuterol, alfuzosin, amiodarone, amisulpride, amitriptyline, amobarbital, amoxapine, anagrelide, apalutamide, apomorphine, arformoterol, aripiprazole, arsenic trioxide, artemether, asenapine, atazanavir, atomoxetine, azithromycin, and other drugs require therapy adjustments, close monitoring, or alternative drug use due to their effects on QTc interval or CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration of bedaquiline with strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors for prolonged periods unless benefits outweigh risks.
